l: creation of the good spirit, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: The creation of the good spirit is directly and indirectly defiled by the living Ashemaogha. A dead stranger does not directly or indirectly defile it in the same manner.

The good spirit's creatures are directly and indirectly defiled by the living Ashemaogha. His actions include striking water, extinguishing fire, carrying off the cow, killing the faithful man, and depriving him of necessities.

The good spirit has creatures including the dog Vanghâpara, which kills thousands of the evil spirit’s creatures from midnight until sunrise. The dog is described as one of the good spirit’s most valuable creatures.
The evil spirit has creatures including the daêva Zairimyangura, which kills thousands of the good spirit’s creatures from midnight until sunrise.

The dog is a creature of the good spirit, valued as a protective watcher over goods, houses, and folds when of sound mind. Its right food is milk, fat, and meat; it ages quickly when not eating near eating people and receiving none of their food. It has characters likened to eight sorts of people: priest, warrior, husbandman, strolling singer, thief, wild beast, courtezan, and child. These characters describe its conduct, from guarding and fighting to singing, prowling, sleeping, and running away. Different kinds receive defined protections, duties, and penalties for injury or death.

Vanghâpara, a dog and good spirit with a prickly back and long, thin muzzle, kills thousands of evil creatures nightly until sunrise. Evil-speaking people call it Duzaka; killing it incurs severe penalties unless atoned through sacrifice to Sraosha.

The shepherd’s dog, one of Ahura Mazda’s two dogs, guards the fold by circling it against thieves and wolves. Together with the house dog it is necessary for every house. It is strongly protected: mistreatment, bad food, exclusion, striking, or killing bring severe guilt or punishment.

A dog belonging to Ahura Mazda guards and supports every house, circling it against thieves and wolves and protecting household goods. Giving it bad food is grave mistreatment, and causing its death brings seven hundred stripes with each of two instruments.
Vohunazga dog is a dog that lacks shepherd’s and house-dog talents, seeks subsistence, and is protected by severe penalties for bad food or death.
Young dogs are supported for six months, becoming capable of self-defence and self-subsistence when able to run around twice seven houses.

The water dog is a dog formed at the spring of the waters from the ghosts of dead dogs and she-dogs, and one is born from a thousand dogs and a thousand she-dogs. Its body and soul part at death. Killing it causes drought, depriving the land of sweetness, fatness, health, healing, and growth until the murderer is killed and a sacrifice is offered.

is_a dog [bites without barking] A mad dog, or one that bites without barking, must be restrained with a wooden collar and tied to a post. If it harms a sheep or a person, its right ear, left ear, right foot, left foot, and finally tail are cut off for successive offenses; if it is not restrained, those responsible incur penalties.

destroys fold [with dogs born of a he-dog and a she-wolf; more murderous, mischievous, and destructive than other wolves] The wolf is treated as a danger against which shepherd’s and house dogs must watch. A wolf born of a he-dog and a she-wolf is said to be more murderous and destructive than one born of a she-dog and a he-wolf, and it deserves more to be killed.
is_supported_for seven years A child is to be supported for seven years.

is_a holy bridge [made by Mazda] The Kinvad bridge is the holy bridge made by Mazda at the head of which souls are asked for the reward of the worldly goods they gave away. The well-shapen maid places the soul of the righteous above the bridge in the presence of the heavenly gods.
A sacrifice to Sraosha atones for killing dog Vanghâpara; after killing a water dog, it is performed for three days and nights with fire, baresma, and Haoma until the land’s blessings return.
is_a fargard Fargard XIV. sets out the penalty and atonement for killing a water dog, as given by Ahura Mazda in answer to Zarathustra.

l: soul of the water dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: The prescribed works, offerings, gifts, and acts of repair are performed as atonement unto the soul of the water dog.

l: penalty for killing a water dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: The penalty for killing a water dog is an atonement made up of punishments, offerings, destruction of harmful creatures, repairs, and gifts. It begins with ten thousand stripes with the Aspahê-astra and ten thousand with the Sraoshô-karana. It requires ten thousand loads each of hard and soft wood for the fire of Ahura Mazda, consecrated baresma, Zaothra libations, and the killing or removal of many creatures and unclean holes. It then requires fire implements, silver, gold, running water, arable land, a house, beds, a virgin maid, cattle, whelps, bridges, repaired stables, and cleansed dogs. It ends with meat, bread, strong drink, and wine sufficient for twice nine godly men, all prescribed as the atonement and penalty for the deed.

Godly men receive implements, war equipment, husbandmen’s tools, land, a house, beds, small cattle, and other provisions as part of the atonement. They are also treated to their fill of meat, bread, strong drink, and wine.

is_worn three years [by a man who follows the law] The sacred girdle is worn by the Âthravan and is required, along with the sacred shirt, for a person over fifteen to avoid being withered by the Daêvas. A person who continues for three years without wearing it, chanting the Gâthas, or worshipping the good waters increases the unseen power of Death.
A rill of running water, as deep and broad as a dog, must be procured to water arable land on both sides.
is_watered_by rill of running water [on both sides] A piece of arable land must be given to godly men. It must be as much land as can be watered with the prescribed rill on both sides.
A house with ox-stalls for godly men is procured with nine hâthras and nine nematas, its parts measuring twelve, nine, and six Vîtâras.

is_a sister or daughter [of the giver; at the age of puberty, with ear-rings, and past her fifteenth year] A virgin maid whom no man has known must be given to a godly man. She is specified as a sister or daughter of the offender, at puberty, with ear-rings, and past her fifteenth year.

l: world of the holy ones, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: The world of the holy ones is entered by anyone who undergoes or pays the prescribed atonement for killing a water dog.
A dark world made of darkness and offspring of darkness. Anyone who fails the prescribed atonement, including one who does not undergo the penalty for killing a water dog, falls into it.

l: godly and piously giving and procuring, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: is atonement [for the soul of the water dog] Godly and pious giving and procuring form a major part of the required atonement. The offender must provide offerings, tools, animals, land, water, buildings, beds, and other goods for godly men and husbandmen.
is_a fargard Fargard XV sets out five sins that make a committer a Peshôtanu and gives teachings about pregnancy, miscarriage, support for pregnant females, and breeding a bitch with three dogs.
Peshôtanu is a penalty status arising from five specified unconfessed, unatoned sins, including suppressing a woman’s issue of blood, and results in two hundred stripes with the Aspahê-astra.

A man incurs grave sin by knowingly teaching a faithful person a foreign wrong creed, harming dogs or pregnant women, or causing a damsel’s miscarriage through an old woman and drugs. He shares the miscarriage sin with them, but if he conceives a child with a damsel, he must support her until birth.

conceives pregnancy [after a man comes near unto her] A damsel who conceives is told not to produce menses against the course of nature or destroy the fruit in her womb from dread of the people. If she causes the fruit to perish, the sin and the murder are on both her and the father, and she pays the penalty for wilful murder.

Woman is described as rich in children, milk, seed, fat, marrow, and offspring. Intercourse with her during bleeding, or while pregnant if harm leads to her death, makes a man a Peshôtanu; later she is made pure and strong.

A bitch big with young must be supported until her whelps are born, with responsibility determined by where she lies. If covered by three dogs, she is watched until she produces a young one and milk; striking her afterward brings seven hundred stripes with each of two instruments.

l: sins that make a committer a Peshôtanu, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: There are five such sins: teaching a faithful person a foreign wrong creed or law knowingly, giving bones or hot food that harms a dog and causes its death, smiting or frightening a pregnant bitch so that she dies, intercourse with a woman who has an issue of blood, and intercourse with a pregnant woman when mischief follows and she dies.

l: teaching a foreign wrong creed, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: Teaching a foreign wrong creed is a sin that makes its teacher a Peshôtanu and increases Death’s unseen power when taught by a man.
Harming a pregnant bitch by smiting or frightening her is a sin; if she dies after falling, the man becomes Peshôtanu and, in a specified condition, incurs seven hundred stripes.

l: intercourse with a menstruating woman, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: Sexual intercourse with a woman who has an issue of blood is condemned as a grave sin; the man who commits it is called ungodly and must pay with his life.

An issue of blood is a condition of a woman that may be ordinary or unusual, occurring out of the ordinary course or at the usual period. Suppressing it incurs stripes, while knowing, willing intercourse with a woman who has it requires the stated atonement.

A man who causes a damsel to conceive must support her until the child is born. Pregnant bitches must likewise be supported until the whelps are born, and Âtar watches over a pregnant bitch as well as over a woman.

Induced miscarriage is murder when a damsel destroys the fruit in her womb. A man may order it from dread of people, and an old woman may use Banga, Shaêta, Ghnâna, Fraspâta, or another drug; the sin falls on all three.

Fargard XV directs the faithful to support every pregnant woman or bitch, assigning responsibility by location and providing foliage bedding for a pregnant bitch until her young can fend for themselves.

is penalty for wilful murder [for failing to support a pregnant female so that the offspring comes to mischief] Failure to support a pregnant damsel or pregnant bitch, when the child or whelps come to mischief for want of proper support, requires payment of the penalty for wilful murder. The damsel and her father also pay that penalty when she destroys the fruit in her womb.

l: breeding a bitch with three dogs, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: A rite for breeding a bitch to produce strong offspring: worshippers of Mazda isolate her in an earth hole, keep three dogs apart, and let them approach her one after another under watch.

Three dogs cover the bitch one after another, each kept apart from the former so that they do not assail one another. The bitch then grows big with young, her milk comes to her teats, and she brings forth a young one born from three dogs.

l: woman who has an issue of blood, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: A woman with an issue of blood is kept in a separate place of infirmity while she continues to see blood. She must remain three paces from worshippers of Mazda and fifteen paces from fire, water, and consecrated bundles of baresma, then is washed with gômêz and water.

is_seen_after three nights [by the woman who has an issue of blood] The woman may continue to see blood after three through nine nights. If she still sees blood after nine nights, the condition is called a work of the Daêvas.
Hair combed or shaved off requires ritual disposal: kept from the faithful, fire, water, and consecrated baresma, then placed in a deep earth-hole with words, furrows, and recitations.

Nails pared off require ritual disposal: bury them in a hole outside the house, as deep as the little finger’s top joint, with spoken words, furrows, Ahuna-Vairya recitations, and dedication to the Ashô-zusta bird. Dedicated nails become weapons; otherwise Mâzainya Daêvas hold them.
is_a rites [required to prevent the production of Daêvas and Khrafstras] The lawful rites must be observed when hair or nails are disposed of. Without them, Daêvas and lice are produced in the earth.
A hole disposes of hair and nails; for hair, its depth varies with whether earth is hard or soft, while for nails it reaches the top joint of the little finger.
Âthravan is a genuine worshipper: girded with sacred law, performing worship, learning and teaching, and staying awake at night seeking holy Wisdom, not merely bearing religious objects.

Paradise is reached by the Âthravan at the head of the Kinvat bridge and by the person who first rises and brings clean wood to Fire. Giving a pair of Parôdars birds or feeding a Parôdars bird also leads directly to paradise.

is_a weapon [best weapon against Angra Mainyu] The sacred Word is one of Zarathustra’s best weapons against Angra Mainyu and his creation. Spenta Mainyu gave it to Zarathustra in the boundless Time, and the Amesha Spentas gave it to him as well.
Parôdars, called Kahrkatâs by ill-speaking people, lifts its voice against dawn, calls people to rise and recite Ashem yad vahistem, and brings blessings.

l: bad thoughts, bad words, and bad deeds, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: are abominable things [three; one must always be slack in them] Bad thoughts, bad words, and bad deeds are three abominable things for which people must always be slack.
Âzi, made by Daêvas, strives against Fire and seeks to put out Fire’s life.

Gahi is a whore addicted to Yâtu, who goes a-whoring after faithful and unfaithful alike; her look and touch wither floods, plants, grass, and the faithful person’s good thoughts, words, deeds, strength, fiend-killing power, and holiness.

Atonement is a prescribed penalty for intercourse with a woman having an issue of blood. It demands vast offerings, consecrations, libations, killings, bridges, and repeated stripes. Payment leads to the world of the holy ones; failure leads to the world of the wicked.

rule the seven Karshvares of the earth [invoked as rulers] The Amesha Spentas give Zarathustra the sacred Word and are invoked as rulers over the seven Karshvares of the earth. They are honored with sacrifice and are associated with their golden seat and Garô-nmânem.

l: the soul of the righteous, Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: A righteous soul, guided after death by the well-shapen maid across the Kinvad bridge, enters Garô-nmânem and is placed before heavenly gods and golden seats.
A graceful, wise maid accompanied by dogs comes to the righteous soul, distinguishes and acts freely, then guides it above Hara-berezati and the Kinvad bridge before the heavenly gods.
Garô-nmânem is the abode of Ahura Mazda, the Amesha Spentas, and holy beings, receiving righteous souls after they reach the golden seat.
Nairyô-sangha, Ahura Mazda’s herald, is sent to Airyaman’s mansion to deliver a request for healing.
Vouru-kasha is the holy gathering sea of waters, from which waters rise, travel aerially, descend to earth, and roll along.

Thrita is the first healer, foremost among the healthful, wise, happy, wealthy, glorious, and strong men of yore. He obtains a source of remedies from Khshathra-Vairya, then drives away sickness, death, pain, fever, disease, rottenness, and infection from mortal bodies.
The Gaini makes sickness and death, and wicked Gainis are driven away. The Gahi is described as addicted to the Yâtu.
Sickness, made by Gaini, is driven back by Thrita and Ahura Mazda, commanded to depart, then destroyed by descending waters with other diseases.
Pain is commanded to depart, and Ahura Mazda says he drives it away.
The fire of fever was turned away from mortal bodies by Thrita. Fever is commanded to depart, and Ahura Mazda says he drives it away.

Diseases created by Angra Mainyu through witchcraft afflict mortal bodies in vast numbered multitudes; commanded to depart, they are driven away by Ahura Mazda and Airyaman along with death, pain, fever, rottenness, and infection.
grow_around Gaokerena [by many hundreds, by many thousands, by many myriads] Ahura Mazda brought down healing plants that grow by many hundreds, thousands, and myriads around Gaokerena.
Thrita asked for a source of remedies and obtained it from Khshathra-Vairya to withstand sickness, death, pain, fever, disease, rottenness, and infection.
Bodies of mortals suffer sickness, death, pain, fever, disease, rottenness, and infection; health is invoked, and Thrita first turns away poniard and fever.
is_a Fargard Fargard XXI concerns waters and light, including their power to bring growth, health, healing, and protection from sickness and death.
The holy bull, beneficent and making increase and growth, bestows gifts on faithful people, including those unborn, before Gahi, Ashemaogha, and a wicked tyrant kill it.
Clouds travel sky and air, descend as countless drops, bring waters, earth, trees, health, healing powers, and destroy sickness and death.
Hara Berezaiti is the place above which the sun, moon, and stars are called to rise and produce light for the world.

keeps_away evil The holy spell keeps away evil by cleansing the birth and growth of a child and making a woman's body and strength pure. It makes the woman rich in children, milk, seed, fat, marrow, and offspring, and causes a thousand springs to flow toward pastures that feed the child.

l: the mansion (made by Ahura Mazda), Vendidad (Vendîdâd)
s: is_a mansion [beautiful, shining, seen afar] The mansion is described as beautiful, shining, and seen afar. Ahura Mazda says that he made it and that he may go up there and pass there.
Mãthra Spenta, the most glorious and all-glorious one, responds to Ahura Mazda’s request for healing by asking how diseases are driven away.

This unit presents Sîrôzah I and II, prayers and sacrifices addressed to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, and many other divine beings. Ahura Mazda is invoked as bright and glorious and as the Maker. The Amesha-Spentas are repeatedly invoked or sacrificed to as beneficent and all-ruling, and each is associated with particular virtues or sacred powers. The text also names waters, plants, stars, winds, Fravashis, mountains, laws, and other beings honored in the prayers.
Ahura Mazda is invoked as bright and glorious and is called the Maker. The prayers and sacrifices are offered to him, and many beings, places, objects, and powers are described as made by Mazda.

The Amesha-Spentas are invoked alongside Ahura Mazda in Sîrôzah I and are sacrificed to as all-ruling and all-beneficent in Sîrôzah II. Individual Amesha-Spentas, including Vohu-Manô, Asha-Vahista, Khshathra-Vairya, Spenta-Ârmaiti, Haurvatât, and Ameretât, are associated with specific virtues, powers, or forms of prosperity.

A sequence of Yasts presents Ahura Mazda’s revelations to Spitama Zarathustra and the worship of powerful holy beings. It begins with the Holy Word: Mazda’s twenty names are declared victorious, healing, and protective, while holiness and good thoughts, words, and deeds are praised. The following units expand worship through sacrifice, prayer, hymns, libations, and blessings to the Amesha-Spentas, especially Asha-Vahista and Haurvatât, whose powers defeat Daêvas, Drug, sickness, Death, the Nasu, and other harms while granting health, prosperity, long life, brightness, and the blissful abode of the holy Ones. The account then turns to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, the holy, health-giving water. Ahura Mazda commands her worship and descent to protect creation; her channels, appearance, attendants, and benefits for fertility, lands, animals, and people are described. Numerous figures seek her aid. She grants boons to Yôista, Zarathustra, Kavi Vîstâspa, Zairi-vairi, Vafra Navâza, and Vistauru, but refuses Aregat-aspa and Vandaremaini’s request to overcome Vîstâspa and Zairi-vairi. The Sun, Moon, and Tistrya are then honored as forces sustaining the created world. The rising Sun cleanses creation and prevents the Daêvas from destroying the seven Karshvares; the Moon preserves the Bull’s seed and fosters spring plants; Tistrya defeats Apaosha so waters, clouds, rain, fertility, health, and protection may reach the Aryan countries. Drvâspa likewise receives sacrifices from figures including Zarathustra and Kavi Vîstâspa for health of flocks, victory, relief, and advancement of Mazda’s law. Mithra dominates the later units as the sleepless, all-seeing lord of wide pastures: guardian, warrior, judge, and protector who observes thoughts, words, deeds, contracts, sacrifices, and lies. He rewards truthful worshippers with prosperity, strength, victory, wisdom, and protection, while defeating enemies and punishing those who lie. Sraosha is similarly invoked as a fiend-smiting defender whose prayer, truth, and Mazda’s law repel wicked forces. The document closes with Rashnu, praised through Mazda’s explanation of the Holy Word as truthful, healthful, wise, and uniquely powerful to destroy evil; Rashnu embodies justice, discernment, and punishment of thieves.

Ahura Mazda is a bright, glorious, holy, most beneficent Spirit: Lord, Maker, creator deity, and creator of the material world and creation. He has strength, vigour, complete knowledge, unde­ceivable understanding of truth, and the will of the Lord. He makes earth, water, the good Waters, plants, wisdom, Saoka, Gaokerena, and beings including Vohu-Manô, Asha-Vahista, Khsathra-Vairya, Spenta-Ârmaiti, Tistrya, Sraosha, and help, comforts, enjoyments, and pleasures for the faithful. Worship, sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, glorification, holiness, and the laws of Ahura surround him; worshippers of Mazda obey those laws and are distinguished from the wicked. He speaks repeatedly as teacher to Spitama Zarathustra, answering questions, revealing names, teaching the Law and ritual practice, explaining Haurvatât and the Amesha-Spentas, and instructing the increase of Asha-Vahista through worship and good thoughts, words, and deeds. He acts through and establishes others: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita descends and keeps holy creation; Zarathustra becomes master of the material world; Tistrya oversees the stars and receives aid against Apaosha; Mithra maintains the moving world; and Sraosha defends against Aêshma. Across the records he is praised and invoked for aid, victorious strength, cleanliness of the earth, protection, truth, and destruction of Angra Mainyu, Daêvas, fiends, and malice.

Angra Mainyu is a fiend, Daêva, and all death: the worst-lying of all Daêvas and an enemy of the good principle. He creates Azi Dahâka and the strongest Drug against the material world to destroy the world of the good principle. Ahura Mazda’s names protect people from him; Asha-Vahista makes him flee in fear. He is afflicted and is destroyed by those who truly do God’s foremost wish.

Zarathustra is a person, a worshipper of Mazda, follower of Ahura Mazda, Zaotar, son of Pourushaspa, master of the material world, and enemy of the Daêvas. He obeys Ahura’s law, the laws of Ahura, and the law of holiness. Addressed by Ahura Mazda as Spitama Zarathustra, he repeatedly asks for knowledge: the strongest and healing part of the Holy Word, right words for worship, teachings about Haurvatât, Tistrya, libations to Mithra, prayer, the Law, and what is true and destructive of evil. He receives instructions to recite names, use words of protection, observe ritual requirements, and limit disclosure of the spell. He is charged with crushing Yâtus, confronting Drug, restoring Mazda’s Law, and acting through worship and sacred deeds. He reports overcoming a ruffian through Spenta-Ârmaiti. He offers sacrifices, especially in Airyana Vaêgah by the good river Dâitya, asks how to worship Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and Tistrya, and seeks to bring Kavi Vîstâspa and Hutaosa to think, speak, and act according to the law and support the Mazdean law. His words and good deeds, completed and future, are worshipped.

The Amesha-Spentas are holy, all-ruling, all-beneficent beings, described as Ahura Mazda's creatures and the strongest part of the Holy Word. They receive worship through sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification; their help and joy are invoked. Their sevenfold presence protects against enemies, and their names are said to smite men turned to Nasus by the Druges. They include Vohu-Manô, Asha-Vahista, Khshathra-Vairya, Spenta-Ârmaiti, Haurvatât, and Ameretât. They have shining, beautiful abodes, can go along the seven Karshvares, and are linked with a way made easy through proclaiming Asha-Vahista. They also hold the Moon’s glory and pour it upon Mazda's earth.

Holy Word is the strongest, most victorious, glorious, effective, fiend-smiting, and best-healing part of religious knowledge. Its part consists of Ahura Mazda’s names. It heals the faithful and enables conversation with God through revelation. As the best-healing remedy, it is true, progress-making, discerning, healthful, wise, happy, and more powerful in destruction than all other creatures.
Good thoughts, words, and deeds are praised and embraced, while evil counterparts are rejected in association with God’s foremost wish.
Ashem Vohû is a prayer declaring holiness the best of all good, identifying it with holy law and repeatedly praising, worshipping, and perfecting it through holy ones.
Worshippers of Mazda obey Ahura’s laws and follow the truest-giving Law; through good thoughts, words, and deeds, Sraosha protects faithful people, houses, and communities receiving sacrifice.

Daêvas are evil, fiendish beings born of darkness, associated with malice and counted in numberless myriads. They are objects of hatred for Mazda-worshippers and are opposed under the laws of Ahura by worshippers of Mazda, heavenly Yazatas, Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, and other faithful forces. From the beginning, Ahura Mazda’s names are invoked to destroy their malice and afflict them; speakers declare hatred of them and seek their crushing. The Airyaman prayer and Asha-Vahista defeat and smite them, while Haurvatât’s name is invoked against their vast numbers. They appear in conflicts involving the Daêvas of Mâzana and are feared as a threat so great that, if the sun did not rise, they would destroy all things in the seven Karshvares. Though they receive libations after sunset, they are portrayed howling and shouting. Mithra makes them flee in fear, and Sraosha drives them away, forces them to bow, or sends them into darkness. Good prayer, truth, and the Law of Mazda-worshippers ultimately smite or destroy them.

Vohu-Manô is a creature of Ahura Mazda and an Amesha-Spenta. Associated with riches for those who work for Mazda and relieve the poor, it comes with Sraosha to help those Ahura Mazda pleases, receives worship, and opposes its destroyer through preaching and smiting.

Asha-Vahista is a creature of Ahura Mazda, the fairest Amesha-Spenta, worshipped as undying and beneficent. Hymns and sacrifice increase and honor him, praising his brightness, glory, strength, and vigour. He is invoked with holy creations and at Gâh Rapithwin, and smites sickness, Death, Daêvas, counter-work, Ashemaogha, and oppressors.
is_a creature of Ahura Mazda Khsathra-Vairya is named among the creatures of Ahura Mazda.

Spenta-Ârmaiti is a good creature of Ahura Mazda, named among holy creation. Associated with the good Râta, she receives sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification; through her eyes or help, ruffians and enemies are made powerless and their malice shattered.

Haurvatât is an Amesha-Spenta and master of prosperity and holiness, a reward for holy ones freed from their bodies. It provides help, comforts, and pleasures for the faithful, receives extensive offerings and worship, and confesses Mithra's religion.

Sraosha is a good, holy god and master of holiness: tall-formed, strong, fiend-smiting, incarnate Word, and mighty-speared. Invoked with Ahura Mazda’s invocation, he comes for help and joy, and with Vohu-Manô helps those whom Ahura Mazda pleases. He makes the world and material world grow, maintains and watches over them, and is the poor’s best protector. Never sleeping, he guards Mazda’s creation, protects faithful people and houses, and stands with his uplifted club from sunset. Every day and night he fights Mâzainya Daêvas, does not bow before Daêvas, and is linked with Peace, Rashnu Razista, Ashi Vanguhi, and Mithra. Offerings and prayers honor his holiness, brightness, glory, strength, and victorious power through all his moments.

Drug is an evil, fiendish, world-destroying being, three-mouthed, three-headed, six-eyed, and possessing a thousand senses. It comes into the Aryan countries through open, hidden, and contact-defiling ways, defiling men and turning them toward Nasus. The spell’s speaker binds, smites, throws down, and drives it away. Good prayer, marked by Manly Courage without deceit or harm, turns it away. Sraosha watches over and fights it, while Thraêtaona seeks and gains power to overcome the powerful Drug, identified with Azi Dahâka and created by Angra Mainyu against the material world.
The faithful gain Ahura Mazda’s increase and Mithra’s help; arriving at the appointed time, he protects and grants virtue, prosperity, strength, victory, wisdom, and bliss.
is_a place [where Zarathustra offered sacrifice] Airyana Vaêgah is the place where Zarathustra offers Drvâspa a sacrifice by the good river Dâitya.

Tistrya is a bright, glorious star and powerful seed of the waters, bringing waters, rain, fertility, health, and protection to the material world. A lord of a thousand boons, he grants male children, oxen, and horses to those offering libations with Haoma and holy meat. Traveling from the shining east by a watery way, he appears successively as a fifteen-year-old man, a golden-horned bull, and a white horse. At Vouru-Kasha he fights and overcomes Daêva Apaosha, drives back Pairikas, binds Duzyâirya, boils the sea, and sends vapours, clouds, rain, and waters toward the seven Karshvares.

The material world, made by Ahura Mazda, gains fulfilment of its wishes and freedom from heart anxiety through the Holy Word. Tistrya brings waters, rain, clouds, and fertility and guards its life from hostile forces. It contains Mithra’s dwelling, while Sraosha protects and oversees the moving world, fighting the Mâzainya Daêvas.

Sacrifice and prayer are offerings to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, Haurvatât, Tistrya, and other holy beings, made with propitiation and glorification. They include libations, Haoma, baresma, meat, spoken words, deeds, and for Tistrya a same-coloured head of cattle. They seek blessings, protection, health, prosperity, strength, and Tistrya’s timely arrival; some people are forbidden from taking part.

l: the names of Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: Ahura Mazda’s twenty names are revealed, including the Herd-giver, Perfect Holiness, Understanding, Knowledge, Weal, AHURA, the Creator, and MAZDA; reciting and pronouncing them by day or night protects a person from foes, weapons, fiends, malice, and harm.
is_a livestock [kept in health by Drvâspa] Drvâspa keeps the flocks in health, and Yima Khshaêta asks her to bring fatness and flocks down to the world created by Mazda.

Mithra is a holy, heavenly, powerful, all-knowing god and the lord of wide pastures, also lord of all countries. Sleepless and ever awake, he has a thousand ears, many senses, ten thousand eyes, and ten thousand powerful, undeceivable spies. Ahura Mazda made his dwelling on Hara Berezaiti, from which Mithra surveys the material world; after sunset he surveys everything between earth and heavens. He is keeper and maintainer of all creatures and maintains Mazda’s creation without sleeping. Mithra protects those who do not lie, but withholds strength and glory from those who lie unto him. Kings, poor men deprived of their rights, and cows driven astray invoke him. At his will he gives boons and pasture-fields, and as a boon grants riches, strength, and victory. He destroys malice among Daêvas, men, Yâtus, Pairikas, and oppressors; yet in his might he can impart brightness and glory as well as sickness, death, poverty, and sterility to those who anger or offend him. He is accompanied or assisted by Sraosha, Nairyô-sangha, Rashnu, Rashnu-Razista, Kista, Âtar, and the Fravashis of the faithful. He has friendship with Verethraghna. Protected and associated with the Law of Mazda, Mithra travels between Karshvares in high-wheeled, heavenly, golden, ever-swift chariots drawn by four white, shining, beneficent, knowledgeable steeds. Armed with a hundred-knotted, hundred-edged club and strong long arms, he is feared by Angra Mainyu, Aêshma, Bûshyãsta, Daêvas, and Varenya fiends. Worshipped with sacrifice, proper words, and consecrated libations, he increases the creation of Spenta Mainyu and shines like the moon when making his body shine.

is_made_by Ahura Mazda [holy waters] Water flows from Ardvi Sûra Anâhita across the seven Karshvares, both in summer and winter. Her waters purify seed and wombs, provide milk, and can be made partly still or partly flowing to create a dry passage.

l: the Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: The Law of the worshippers of Mazda is worshipped and is the will of the Lord. It is identified with holiness, governing sacrifice, prayer, and invocations, which must follow holiness’s perfection. Named with the waters made by Mazda and among recipients of sacrifice, it is fiend-destroying and the truest giver of good things, whose offspring belong to the good principle.

The Law of Mazda is a captive power in the hands of the ungodly, recoverable by one who destroys Vohu-Manô’s destroyer. It is closely associated with Mithra, opening his way and making his strength ten thousandfold, though scorned by an unholy priest.

Sacrifice is a ritual offering and act of worship made repeatedly to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, the Sun, the Moon, Drvâspa, Mithra, Sraosha, the worshipper's soul, and other holy beings. It is blessed with prayer, strength, and vigour, and seeks prosperity, well-being, brightness, glory, protection, victory, wisdom, bliss, and good conscience. It may begin with prayer, propitiation, and glorification, and includes libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, speech, deeds, wisdom of the tongue, and rightly-spoken or proper words; it may also include cattle, birds, and Haomas. Offerings to the Sun seek resistance to darkness, hostile beings, robbers, and unseen death. Offerings to the Moon address its bulls and moons. Offerings to Mithra ask acceptance, loving gathering, and placement in the Garô-nmâna; a pious priest pleases Mithra, unlike an unholy priest. Sacrifice concludes with the blessing of the sacrifice and prayer of Sraosha.

Prayer is an act of worship and ritual utterance offered with sacrifice, propitiation, and glorification to Ahura Mazda, holy beings, and figures including Asha-Vahista, Drvâspa, and Sraosha. It uses hymns, invocations, holy words, blessings, and adoration; it is blessed with strength and vigour, increases Asha-Vahista, and is associated with protection from fiends.

The Law of holiness is the will of the Lord and Ahura Mazda, called the best of all good. It is stated in the Yathâ ahû vairyô formula, while holiness is named the best of all good in the Ashem Vohû formula. It follows worship and the crushing of evil, offers healing, and is followed by the faithful to still the Druges. It is spread and made known by Hutaosa, as requests are made to bring nations to the good law.
Brightness and glory are offered to Mithra through sacrifice and sought as blessings for faithful man, whom Mithra can impart them to when worshipped and satisfied.
is_a Yast It presents teachings and praises concerning Asha-Vahista, the Airyaman prayer, healing, and the defeat of harmful forces.
Garô-nmâna is Ahura Mazda’s abode for holy souls, with bright holy ways barred to every wicked person.
is_a unholy being The unholy Ashemaogha flees before the Airyaman prayer and is smitten and afflicted by Asha-Vahista.
A greatest, fairest, firm, victorious, healing spell and best-healing remedy that smites Angra Mainyu’s creatures and drives away sickness, Death, Daêvas, and harmful forces.
is_smitten_by Airyaman prayer Sickness flees before the Airyaman prayer and is smitten by Asha-Vahista. The prayer is said to drive sickness away from the body of the faithful.
Death, opposed by Sun sacrifice, flees Airyaman prayer and is smitten by Asha-Vahista; Angra Mainyu is all death.
Sacrifice praises and increases Asha-Vahista, invokes the Amesha-Spentas, and offers libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, speech, deeds, and rightly-spoken words.
The Airyaman prayer is described as the greatest, fairest, most fearful, firmest, most victorious, and best-healing of spells. Its power drives away sickness, Death, Daêvas, and other harmful forces.

Rashnu Razista is a holy, tall, strong, true, just, beneficent, knowledgeable being associated with Sraosha. He administers justice, smites thieves, destroys bandits, and watches men worldwide. Praised and invoked, his friendship is sought for a prepared var and offerings; sacrifice, prayer, strength, and vigour are blessed for him.
Heavenly Yazatas, hundreds and thousands, rise as the sun grows warmer, gather the Sun's Glory, pass it down onto Ahura's earth, and rejoice in sacrifice to the Sun.

The faithful man is the first of men. Rashnu Razista, the male heavenly Yazatas, and the Amesha-Spentas free him from the Nasu, harmful beings, wicked men, and other threats. Protected by Sraosha, his houses are rich in good thoughts, good words, and good deeds. He separates himself from the wicked by pronouncing Ahura Mazda’s spell and drawing three, six, or nine furrows.

is_a defiling being [smitten by the names of the Amesha-Spentas] The Nasu is smitten by invoking Haurvatât and by the names of the Amesha-Spentas. It is struck with bruising and deadly blows after the sun goes down for the propitiation and glorification of the heavenly gods.

Aryan countries depend on Tistrya for fertility, rain, and flowing waters; through sacrifice, prayer, and invocation, they receive rain and protection from hostile hordes, plagues, leprosy, venomous plants, and enemy weapons.

l: the law of holiness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: Holiness is the best of all good and the law of the Lord. It is associated with Haurvatât, seasonal prosperity, and years, then with increasing the world and its creatures, and finally with the Moon, its seed of the Bull, and mastery of holiness.

Holy spells are recited by heart and taught only through restricted family or Âthravan-to-qualified-pupil transmission. The spell smites, binds, and throws down the Drug, separating the faithful’s way from the wicked’s way.
Mithra’s red, strong golden-brass club, with a hundred knots and edges, is the strongest victorious weapon, carried to rush forward and strike down men and Daêvas.

Haoma is an enlivening, healing, fair, lordly, golden-eyed being. On the highest height of Haraiti Bareza or Hara Berezaiti, Haoma offers sacrifices to Drvâspa and Mithra, using undefiled implements, libations, words, and heavenly-mortared Haomas, while asking that Franghrasyan be bound and brought to Husravah.

is_offered_to Haurvatât [as part of propitiation and glorification] Prayer is joined with sacrifice, propitiation, and glorification for Hâvani, Haurvatât, the prosperity of the seasons, and the years. The Yathâ ahû vairyô and Ashem Vohû prayers are recited or invoked.

Ardvi Sûra Anâhita is a wide-expanding, health-giving, holy spring, river, and water. She hates the Daêvas, obeys Ahura Mazda’s laws, and preserves Ahura Mazda’s whole holy creation. Flowing from Hukairya to Vouru-Kasha and through the seven Karshvares, she is the source of their waters, with a thousand cells and channels. Her waters increase life, herds, folds, wealth, and countries; purify male seed and female wombs; and put milk into females’ breasts in the proper measure. Bright and glorious, she appears as a powerful, pure, high-girded maid, wearing a gold-embroidered mantle and beaver garments, and travels with four horses: wind, rain, cloud, and sleet. Worthy of sacrifice and prayer, she is worshipped by Ahura Mazda, Hvôvas, and Naotaras. She waits for libations and prayers, granting boons to worthy supplicants, such as Vîstâspa and Zairi-vairi, while also refusing some requests. She rescues Vafra Navâza and aids Vistauru.

l: waters that run along the earth, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: become clean [when the sun rises] The good Waters are made by Mazda and receive propitiation with sacrifice, prayer, and glorification. They are associated with Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and with all waters made by Mazda.

Libations are ritual offerings that must be cleanly prepared, well strained, and properly offered, often with Haoma, meat, sacrifice, gifts, prayers, and entreaties. They accompany requests for boons from Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and Drvâspa, may please Mithra, and give him strength and energy. Qualified Âthravan priests may drink them after prescribed washing, strokes, and knowledge of the staota yêsnya; offerings after sunset are received by Daêvas.

Sacrifice is repeatedly offered to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita with prayers, libations, gifts, Haoma, meat, baresma, spells, words, and deeds. Ahura Mazda and human figures perform it to propitiate and glorify her, then request favor, victory, prosperity, knowledge, husbands, safe delivery, horses, and other boons.

A boon is a requested favor obtained through sacrifice and entreaty. Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and Drvâspa grant boons to many figures for sovereignty, victory, rescue, safe passage, and aid, while Ardvi Sûra Anâhita refuses certain requesters.

Vouru-Kasha is a powerful, large, deep sea of salt waters. Ardvi Sûra Anâhita runs into it from Hukairya; its shores and middle boil, holding Mount Us-hindu and the tree of the eagle. Frangrasyan seeks Aryan Glory there, Keresâspa opposes Gandarewa, and Tistrya fights Apaosha, rises with Satavaêsa, and sends its waters toward material countries.
Hukairya is a golden height with deep precipices, from which Ardvi Sûra Anâhita runs and leaps toward Vouru-Kasha, descending with great force and Glory; Yima Khshaêta offers sacrifice to her there.
Seven regions receiving Ardvi Sûra Anâhita’s waters and containing all things; Azi Dahâka seeks to empty them of men, but is refused.

is_a lake [deep and of salt waters] The Kaêkasta lake is described as a deep lake of salt waters. Haoma asks that Franghrasyan be brought there, and Husravah offers a sacrifice behind it and asks to kill him there.
Haoshyangha, the Paradhâta, sacrifices to Drvâspa on Hara’s enclosure and gains fearlessness to overcome Mâzana’s Daêvas.

is_a good shepherd Yima Khshaêta, the good shepherd, sacrifices to Drvâspa from the height Hukairya. He asks for fatness, flocks, and immortality and for the removal of hunger, thirst, old age, death, hot wind, and cold wind from the Mazda-created world for a thousand years.

Thraêtaona, valiant heir of the Âthwya clan, sacrifices to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and Drvâspa, seeking strength to overcome Azi Dahâka and rescue Savanghavâk and Erenavâk; Ardvi Sûra Anâhita grants the boon, and he overcomes Azi Dahâka.
The Aryan people possess Glory, include those born and not yet born, and are united by Husravah into one kingdom; their enemies are defeated through requests to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita.
Husravah is a gallant king who united the Aryan nations into one kingdom, sacrifices to Drvâspa to avenge Syâvarshâna and Aghraêratha, and is asked to kill the bound Franghrasyan.

l: the earth made by Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: The earth made by Ahura is wide, round, and far-reaching; at sunrise it becomes clean as heavenly Yazatas pour the Sun's Glory for holiness, while Mithra travels, surveys, and encompasses all its regions.

Kavi Vîstâspa, son of Aurvat-aspa, is a tall Kavi, a Naotaride, and lord of the swiftest horses. Ardvi Sûra Anâhita grants him victory-related boons and is invoked to guide him toward the law. He sacrifices to Drvâspa, seeking defeat of enemies and conversion of Varedhakas and Hvyaonas.

is_denied favour [by Ardvi Sûra Anâhita] Aregat-aspa is described as wicked and as a worshipper or follower of the bad law. Ardvi Sûra Anâhita grants a boon against him to Kavi Vîstâspa and Zairi-vairi, but refuses his own request, made with Vandaremaini, to conquer Vîstâspa and Zairi-vairi.

Zairi-vairi is a mounted fighter who offers a sacrifice to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and receives the boon of overcoming Peshô-Kangha, Humâyaka, and the wicked Aregat-aspa. He is later named as one of the Aryan opponents whom Aregat-aspa and Vandaremaini fail to conquer.

Rain follows the vapours and clouds that move from the sea Vouru-Kasha toward the fields and the seven Karshvares. It spreads over the lands and brings healing and fertility when Tistrya has been properly worshipped.

l: undying, shining, swift-horsed Sun, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: The undying, shining, swift-horsed Sun is the Yast’s subject, receiving offerings and worship. Through Glory it increases holiness; when it rises, it cleans earth, waters, and holy creatures, while its light withstands darkness and hostile forces.

become clean [when the sun rises] The waters arise from the sea Vouru-Kasha, are divided among the countries by Apãm Napât, and flow toward fields, pastures, plants, lakes, caves, and channels. Their movement depends on Tistrya’s victory and on the wind, clouds, and rain made by Mazda.

l: Moon that keeps in it the seed of the Bull, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: The Moon, holy and master of holiness, keeps the seed of the Bull. It waxes for fifteen days, warming its light so golden-hued plants grow, then wanes for fifteen days. Bright and glorious, it gives water, warmth, wisdom, wealth, healing, and prosperity, and receives libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, speech, and deeds.
Daêva Apaosha, a dark horse of terror, meets Tistrya at sea Vouru-Kasha, defeats him after three days and nights, then is overcome when Tistrya gains strength through sacrifice.

Fertility comes to the Aryan countries through Tistrya’s waters and rain. The waters reach big-seeded cornfields, small-seeded pasture-fields, beautiful places, fields, pastures, and the roots of plants so that they grow powerfully.

l: battle between Tistrya and Apaosha, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: Tistrya and the Daêva Apaosha fight at the sea Vouru-Kasha in the forms of white and dark horses. Apaosha first overcomes Tistrya after three days and three nights, but Tistrya later defeats him by noon after receiving the strength of ten horses, camels, bulls, mountains, and rivers.

For ten nights Tistrya appears in the shape of a fifteen-year-old man, for the next ten nights in the shape of a golden-horned bull, and for the following ten nights as a white, beautiful horse with golden ears and a golden caparison. He goes to the sea Vouru-Kasha in the horse shape.

Drvâspa is a powerful, holy maintainer made by Mazda who keeps flocks, herds, cattle, and young ones healthy, assists the faithful, yokes horses and has a sounding-wheeled chariot, then grants boons to entreating sacrificers.
Bright mountain around which many stars revolve, free from night and darkness; Mithra dwells there, unreachable by clouds, and Haoma sacrifices on its highest heights.
is_a Turanian murderer Franghrasyan is identified as a Turanian murderer. Haoma asks that he be bound and brought to Husravah, and Husravah asks to kill him behind the Kaêkasta lake.
Hutaosa, a good and noble woman, is asked by Zarathustra to follow, spread, and praise the Mazdean law.

l: those who lie unto Mithra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: Those who lie unto Mithra are punished by Mithra: they lose strength, swiftness, eyesight, hearing, glory, vigour, and boons. Their weapons fail, homes and communities become desolate, fear, defeat, and death come upon them, and their bodies may be destroyed in battle.

must_not_be_broken Mithra [whether made with faithful or unfaithful] The text warns that a contract must not be broken, whether it is made with an unfaithful person or with a faithful person. Mithra stands for both the faithful and the unfaithful.

is_a good [the principle invoked in the sacrifice] Mithra is described as truth-speaking and as one who sees every man who tells a lie. He punishes men who lie unto him and is associated with observing evil thoughts, words, and deeds.

In battle, Mithra confronts armies, breaks their lines, spreads terror, and causes weapons to miss their marks. He supports those who honor him and brings defeat, slaughter, and flight upon hostile forces and those who lie unto him.

Mithra is asked to dash in pieces the malice of malicious men and the malice of the malicious. He is also asked to smite all the malice of Daêvas, men, Yâtus, Pairikas, oppressors, the blind, and the deaf.

is_drawn_by white stallions [four, all of the same white colour] Mithra drives a beautiful, swift golden chariot from the shining Garô-nmâna. Four white, undying stallions draw it, and it bears Rashnu-Razista, Kista, Âtar, the kingly Glory, and numerous bows, arrows, spears, hammers, swords, maces, and a club.

l: the creation of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII
s: is_guarded_by Sraosha [wakefully and without sleeping] The creation of Mazda is guarded and maintained by Sraosha, who watches over it without sleeping. Sraosha protects it with his club uplifted from the hour when the sun is down.
Good prayer is excellent for the worlds: without deceit or harm, it protects people in danger by taking away fiends’ friendship and faculties and driving away the Drug.
The var prepared is an object toward which Ahura Mazda and Rashnu are invoked to show friendship, associated with fire, baresma, full boiling milk, oil, and plant sap.

This collection of Yasts and related blessings presents Ahura Mazda’s teaching to Zarathustra and the worship of powerful holy beings, especially the Fravashis of the faithful. The Fravashis sustain creation, protect families, towns, rulers, waters, plants, animals, and unborn children, defeat Daêvas and enemies, and bless those who honor them with sacrifice, prayer, food, clothing, and devotion. The texts praise the good Law of the worshippers of Mazda, holiness, good thoughts, words, and deeds, and figures including Gaya Maretan, Zarathustra, Vîstâspa, Haoshyangha, Yima, Thraêtaona, Keresâspa, and many holy men and women. Other units invoke Verethraghna, Vayu, Kista, Ashi Vanguhi, the Aryan Glory, kingly Glory, and the star Vanant for victory, health, wealth, strength, wisdom, prosperity, protection, and healing. Verethraghna takes many forms and supplies battle protection; Vayu grants boons while rejecting Azi Dahâka’s destructive request; Ashi Vanguhi gives glory and prosperity but condemns sexual and reproductive wrongdoing. The Glory moves among mountains, rulers, heroes, Zarathustra, and the Aryan nations, supporting Vîstâspa’s advance of the Law and defeat of enemies. The collection repeatedly opposes Angra Mainyu, the Drug, Daêvas, Yâtus, Khrafstras, and wicked people. It looks ahead to Saoshyant and Astvat-ereta, who will raise and restore the bodily world: death, decay, hunger, thirst, the Drug, and Angra Mainyu will perish, and living creatures will reach immortality. Its closing teachings concern worship and moral consequence. Praise of Holiness is the glorification of all Mazda’s good creations, especially when joined to professions of good thoughts, words, and deeds and rejection of evil. After death, faithful souls pass through paradises to Endless Lights, while wicked souls descend through hells to Endless Darkness. Zarathustra’s blessings for Vîstâspa and his teachings to the young king culminate in prosperity, righteous rule, charity, proper worship, the defeat of evil, and entry into Garô-nmâna, the bright abode of the holy Ones.

Ahura Mazda is a Lord, creator, ruler, Maker, heavenly god, Good Spirit, and the greatest and best of all gods. He is the most beneficent Spirit and Maker of the material world, with a Fravashi praised as supreme in holiness and in many excellences. Through the brightness and glory of the Fravashis of the faithful, he establishes and maintains the sky, waters, earth, and plants; he makes the earth wide and broad, the waters, and Victory. He is father and commander of the seven Amesha-Spentas, father of Ashi Vanguhi, maker of Vanant, and creator of Verethraghna. He formed Aryan nations through Gaya Maretan and made the Aryan Glory, Ashi Vanguhi, and the strong wind. He teaches and speaks to Spitama Zarathustra and Zarathustra, whose follower and worshipper is identified in the records, including revelations of his Law. He directs worship, hymns, sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, offerings, invocations, and rites, including those concerning Verethraghna. He sacrifices to Vayu and receives Vayu's help against the creation of Angra Mainyu. His Law is upheld by Vîstâspa, made for worshippers of Mazda, and obeyed by a worshipper of Mazda.

Zarathustra is a pure, holy Spitama and Âthravan presented as the foremost mortal and religious leader of the material world. He is the first thinker, speaker, and doer of what is good; the first Priest, Warrior, and Plougher; and the first to know and teach Mazda’s good creations. He possesses Bull, Holiness, the Word, dominion, and kingly Glory, follows and proclaims the Law of Ahura and Mazda, praises Asha, worships Mazda and the faithful Fravashis, and rejects the Daêvas. His birth and growth bring joy to waters, plants, and good creations, while his word and song drive the Daêvas beneath the earth. He is described as lord and master of the world, wisest, best-ruling, brightest, most glorious, and uniquely worthy of sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification. He receives revelation and instruction from Ahura Mazda, including teachings about Glory, the faithful and wicked after death, words of holiness, remedies, and Verethraghna. He invokes powers for danger and battle, makes sacrifices with libations and baresma, and seeks righteousness in thought, speech, and deed, along with speed, strength, health, and exceptional sight. Zarathustra’s work unfolds as the spread and teaching of the good Law throughout the seven Karshvares. He teaches Vîstâspa and others about holiness, worship, sacrifice, charity, the defeat of evil, and the faithful soul’s path to Garô-nmâna. He also blesses Vîstâspa with long life, welfare, victory, virtues, and freedom from sickness and death. Across the records, he appears as a holy worshipper, recipient of divine instruction, destroyer of the Daêvas’ influence, and bearer of a Law that directs thought, speech, action, and the good life.

l: Fravashis of the faithful, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: The Fravashis of the faithful are awful, overpowering, holy, beneficent, undecaying beings belonging to the Amesha-Spentas and greater than words can express. They help Ahura Mazda with vigour, strength, glory, help, and joy, preserve the material world, and maintain the sky, waters, earth, cattle, plants, and unborn children through brightness and glory. They give victory, health, glory, prosperity, and protection to faithful invokers, the sick, worthy sovereigns, houses, and those in distress. During Hamaspathmaêdha they come and go through boroughs for ten nights, seeking sacrifice, prayer, food, and clothing. They seek and bring water for kindred, boroughs, towns, and countries; fight for their own lands; and appear as watchful warriors or well-winged birds rushing to help. They serve as weapons and shields, protecting against the Drug, fiends, evil-doers, Angra Mainyu, and weapons. Associated with perception, intellect, and conscience, and belonging to the Saoshyants, they stood firm at the creation of the world and, with Vohû Manô and Âtar, destroyed Angra Mainyu. They are protected by Ahura Mazda and Sraosha and are asked to carry hymns and worship to Ahura Mazda and the Amesha-Spentas.

Ardvi Sura Anahita is a holy, life-giving river, sustained by the Fravashis, obeying Ahura’s laws and opposing the Daêvas; from Hukairya she flows to Vouru-Kasha, purifying and supplying seven Karshvares.

Mithra is a god and lord of wide pastures and all countries, marked by vast senses and spies. Associated with Rashnu and Verethraghna among armies, he seizes kingly Glory after it first departs from Yima.
A creative spirit fixes and maintains creation, including sky, waters, earth, cattle, plants, and unborn children; faithful Fravashis support the sky after it is fixed.

Ashi Vanguhi is a shining, high, tall-formed, fair, powerful, healing, welfare-giving maid and great Ashi, worthy of sacrifice. Daughter of Ahura Mazda and sister to the Amesha-Spentas, Sraosha, Rashnu, Mithra, and the Law of the worshippers of Mazda, she has a loud-sounding chariot and far-piercing rays. She gives glory, prosperity, heavenly wisdom, and enlivening intelligence to Saoshyants and those she follows or who invoke her. Made by Ahura Mazda, she enters the household and royal palace of a gift-giving faithful man, bringing welfare, flocks, victory, intelligence, and Aryan Glory. She rejects libations from specified people and laments sexual or reproductive wrongdoing.

Keresâspa is a Sâma, club-bearer with plaited hair, manly-hearted and exceptionally strong. Invoked against destructive forces, he withstands a brigand and evil, seizes kingly Glory after it leaves Yima, and with Manly Courage kills Srvara, Gandarewa, hostile broods, Snâvidhaka, and other enemies.

Daêvas are evil creations, fiends, demons, and oppressors opposed to the law of Mazda and Ahura. They assault and oppress the stars, prevent their movement, oppose the faithful Fravashis, and act with worshippers who spill blood and misuse offerings. They are hated by Zarathustra and resisted by the Fravashis, Vayu, Verethraghna, Vîspa-taurvairi, Zarathustra, and the holy Law. Across the records, their malice and strength are broken, they are driven back and beneath the earth by the Ahuna Vairya, deprived of sacrifice and prayer, retire before king Vîstâspa, and are destined to perish with the Drug.

The Drug is a fiendish evil power created by Angra Mainyu against the material world, associated with domination and destruction. She opposes and rushes to kill holy beings, but is driven before the holy religion as king Vîstâspa expands it. In the future, she and her hundredfold evil brood perish when creation becomes deathless.

The Aryan nations are a united kingdom associated with Husravah and the Glory. They are instructed to honor Verethraghna with libations, baresma, cattle, sacrifice, and prayer; proper observance protects their countries from hostile forces, disease, and weapons. The Glory preserves their lands, animals, welfare, and faithful Law against Frangrasyan.

The faithful receive victory, health, good glory, protection, and prosperity through the Fravashis. The Fravashis turn toward places where faithful people are devoted to holiness and are not ill-treated.

l: the men of the primitive law, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: The men of the primitive law are worshipped across houses, boroughs, towns, and countries as past, present, and future occupants, credited with obtaining houses, holiness, Mãthra, the soul’s blessedness, and every perfection of goodness.

The bodily world contains the living and dead; Fravashis preserve its sky, waters, earth, plants, animals, and people against the Drug, until SAOSHYANT benefits it and ASTVAT-ERETA raises its creatures to withstand destruction.
The sky, a shining heavenly structure encompassing the earth, is fixed by Ahura Mazda and Spenta-Mainyu and supported below by the Fravashis.
Earth, worthy of sacrifice, bears the bodily world and is maintained through the brightness and glory of the Fravashis.

Vouru-Kasha is a sea whose shores and middle boil as Ardvi Sura Anahita flows into it. Its arms form Lake Husravah, Lake Vanghazdau, and Awz-dânva. Guarded by countless Fravashis, it receives the Glory after its escape; the Son of the Waters seizes it while Frangrasyan repeatedly fails.

l: seven Karshvares of the earth, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: Seven regions and divisions of the earth are ruled by kings possessing Glory; Frangrasyan attempts to seize it to rule them all.

is_protected_by Fravashis of the faithful [when its sovereign invokes them and has not harmed or offended them] The country is sought and defended by the Fravashis of the faithful. They ask that their country have a good store and full joy, and those who win battles bring waters to it and say, 'May my country grow and increase!'.
The Endless Lights are where the faithful person’s soul arrives after its fourth step.

Waters, created by Ahura Mazda, flow from Ardvi Sura Anahita across the seven Karshvares and rise from sea Vouru-Kasha with Mazda-made Glory. They follow Mazda-appointed paths, maintained and beautified by Fravashis, nourish animals, people, and plants, reach communities, and continue flowing after Angra Mainyu’s malice is destroyed.

Plants grow from earth by never-failing springs, continue growing after Angra Mainyu’s malice is destroyed, are created by Ahura Mazda, and flourish through the Fravashis to nourish animals and people.

l: the good restoration of the world, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: The good restoration of the world is a restoration performed by Saoshyant and helpers, with blessed beings bringing it about. It unfolds as the dead rise, life and immortality come, and the world becomes ever-living, deathless, free from decay and death, increasing, and master of its wish.

Sacrifice is an act of worship and ritual offering, made with prayer, propitiation, and glorification to figures including the Fravashis, Verethraghna, Vayu, Kista, the good Law, and Ahura Mazda's creation. It requires rites and offerings such as libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, words, deeds, and worthy prayer. Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, and others offer it to seek favor and particular boons. When properly performed in holiness, it brings blessings, healing, protection, strength, victory, royalty, and advancement; worshippers become good in Ahura Mazda's eyes. Sacrifice during Hamaspathmaêdha brings blessings of animals, people, horses, chariots, and capable leadership. Improper recipients cause its virtues to be withdrawn.
is_blessed brightness and glory [through the offering] Prayer is offered to the Fravashis and to holy beings. Zarathustra and the holy men and women are described as worthy of prayer.

l: good Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: The good Law of the worshippers of Mazda is a holy, good, victorious law associated with Zarathustra. It spreads through all seven Karshvares after his sacrifices, and is worshipped through sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification. It supplies good stores and is linked to lawful thought, speech, and action; Zarathustra asks Hutaosa to spread and make it known. It embodies holiness, righteousness, innocence, unconquerable power, and the defeat of enemies. Finally, it is protective and life-giving: it should be supported, proclaimed, practiced, and offered even to the unfriendly, while followers care for the poor and avoid evil conduct.

l: the struggle against evil, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: The struggle against evil is an armed conflict against Daêvas and malicious men. Fravashis resist the Drug, break enemy weapons, aid the faithful, and grant victory; when armies meet, Verethraghna is invoked to destroy hostile forces and disable their senses.

l: awful kingly Glory, made by Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: The awful kingly Glory, made by Mazda, is conquering, health-giving, wise, happy, and not forcibly seizable. It belongs to Zarathustra and the Aryan nations, cleaving first to Yima, then Mithra, Thraêtaona, Keresâspa, and king Vîstâspa. Powerful and victorious, it is sacrificed to for brightness and glory, protects the Aryan nations, restores the world, and is associated with Saoshyant and Astvat-ereta.

Angra Mainyu is the Evil Spirit, also named the Evil One, a destructive, lying, evil-doing being who is all death and full of death without Glory. He breaks into the creation of good holiness and makes an evil creation, including Daêvas, Drug, and Azi Dahâka, powerful fiendish forces against the material world and the good principle. His Khrafstras are called accursed, foul, and most abominable. He struggles over the Glory and is associated with lust, derision, idolatry, rejection of the poor, and other harmful acts. Yet his malice is destroyed by the Fravashis, preserving flowing waters and growing plants. At Zarathustra’s birth he flees from earth, acknowledges Zarathustra can smite and daunt him, and is smitten by Ahuna Vairya and burned by Asha-Vahista through Zarathustra. His influence is ultimately to be kept away.

The faithful person’s own conscience is a noble, beautiful maiden. At the third-night dawn she appears to the faithful soul, identifies herself, and reflects the person’s moral character: good thoughts, words, deeds, religion, and treatment of the faithful and poor. These make her increasingly lovely, honored, victorious, and free from sorrow.
Good Spirit creates prosperous creation, contests Evil One for kingly Glory, and is associated with the world’s future deathlessness.
Holiness, the best of all good, brings prosperity, protection, knowledge, spiritual progress, and passage to blessed abodes.

Âtar, son of Ahura Mazda, is a valiant warrior who fights for kingly Glory and protects the Good Principle. In struggle with Azi Dahâka, it withdraws at a threat, then forces Azi to retreat. Worshipped as Fire, it attacks the Drug and drives away wicked foes with its perfume.

The Amesha-Spentas are seven bright, holy, undecaying beings, united in thought, speech, and deed under their father and commander, Ahura Mazda. They think of good thoughts, words, deeds, and Garô-nmâna; govern, preserve, and will restore Ahura Mazda’s creations. They longed for Zarathustra as lord and master of the world and praiser of Asha. The Fravashis of the faithful carry hymns and worship to them. Invoked for greatness, brightness, glory, plenty, protection, and guidance, they impart brightness and Glory to Vîstâspa and promise Zarathustra the way to the spiritual world and Paradise.
Gaya Maretan, first listener to Ahura Mazda’s thought and teaching, is worshipped as the source from whom Ahura formed the Aryan nations.

Vîstâspa is a holy, valiant, gallant, mighty-speared, lordly king and faithful young man who rules the country. He is defined above all by his commitment to the Law: he thinks, speaks, acts, and professes according to it; serves as the arm and support of the laws of Ahura and Zarathustra; drives the Drug before him; maintains Holiness against fiends; and makes wide room for the holy religion. He offers sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi behind the Dâitya, seeks victory over enemies and the conversion of the Varedhakas and Hvyaonas to the good law, and receives the requested boon. He puts Asta-aurvant to flight and conquers Tãthravant, Peshana, and Aregat-aspa. Zarathustra blesses him as lord of the country with life, welfare, strength, glory, wealth, holiness, victory, and freedom from sickness and death. His blessings include royal power, swift horses, prosperity, ten sons, including priests, warriors, tillers, and one like himself, and kingly Glory made by Mazda. He is taught to uphold the Law, reject bad or unfriendly priests, sacrifice and pray properly, help the poor, and follow the right way.

ASTVAT-ERETA is the future beneficent Saoshyant. Rising from Lake Kãsava as Ahura Mazda’s friend and Vîspa-taurvairi’s son, he knows victorious knowledge and looks upon Paêsis with intelligence and plenty. He makes bodily creatures rise, withstands destruction, Drug, and evil, delivers living creatures to immortality, and is joined by friends who follow the good law.
Sraosha is a holy, powerful incarnate Word and god of Asha whose assistance protects people in distress.
Garô-nmâna is Ahura Mazda’s adorned Paradise in the spiritual world, reached by the faithful through Good Thoughts, Good Words, Good Deeds, and Endless Light.
Asha is a good, excellent principle praised as most great, good, and fair; Zarathustra first pronounces and repeatedly praises it, while Haoma drinking is attended by Asha and Ashi Vanguhi.

The law of Ahura is a revelation and word that destroys the Daêvas. Praised as righteous, innocent, and unconquerable, it brings holiness and defeats enemies. Zarathustra first bears it among nations; Vîstâspa supports, professes, and follows it in thought, speech, and action.

SAOSHYANT, the future Beneficent One, benefits and restores the bodily world with helpers, opposing destruction; the world becomes ever living and increasing, the dead rise, and life and immortality come.

Yima, son of Vîvanghant, is a valiant, bright good shepherd whose Fravashi is worshipped against Daêva oppression, pasture-destroying drought, and unseen death. He seeks glory and a reign in which animals and men are undying, waters and plants endure, and food never fails. Vayu and Ashi Vanguhi grant his requests, enabling him to bring fatness, flocks, and immortality to the world and remove hunger, thirst, old age, death, heat, and cold. He rules Varena and the seven Karshvares in abundance, with undrying waters and plants and freedom from deprivation. He possesses the awful kingly Glory until he delights in falsehood and untruth; then the Glory departs as a bird and is later seized by Mithra, Thraêtaona, and Keresâspa.

Thraêtaona is a holy heir of the valiant Âthwya clan and a victorious man. Invoked against itch, fevers, humours, incontinency, and the Serpent’s evil, he rides Vârengana and sacrifices to Ashi Vanguhi at four-cornered Varena. Granted a boon to overcome Azi Dahâka and deliver Savanghavâk and Erenavâk, he seizes the awful kingly Glory after it leaves Yima, kills the fiendish Drug, and bears Mazda-made Glory.

Husravah is a holy, gallant king and unifier of the Aryan nations. After sacrificing to Ashi Vanguhi, he receives a boon to kill Franghrasyan. He gains kingly Glory, strength, victory, health, offspring, long life, and dominion; defeats enemies; and binds Frangrasyan and Keresavazda to avenge Syâvarshâna and Aghraêratha.

is_a keeper [good keeper and maintainer] Strength appears with Victory upon the horns or forehead of some forms of Verethraghna and is called well-shapen and made by Ahura. Strength and Victory are invoked as keepers, maintainers, forgiving and striking powers, and as signs by which victory is determined.

Victory is a good keeper and maintainer that cleaves day after day to Kavi Husravah and those possessing Glory. Accompanying Strength in Verethraghna’s manifestations, it is invoked in battle and martial prayer, enabling conquest of havocking hordes and enemies.

Glory is a blessing made by Mazda, borne by Verethraghna and linked with health, strength, brightness, worship, wealth, and the holy Ones. The Vârengana feather maintains a person's glory, while Verethraghna may confound a house's glory with cattle wealth. Offered and requested with Vayu, it is finally embodied by Ashi Vanguhi and given to those she attends, including Zarathustra's body.

Haoshyangha, a holy and gallant Paradhâta, offers sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi and receives a boon to overcome and terrify the Daêvas of Mâzana; his Fravashi is worshipped to withstand Mâzainya Daêvas, Varenya fiends, and their evil.
Hutaosa, a good and noble Naotara woman, is asked by Zarathustra to follow, spread, and uphold the law while praising his deeds.

Yathâ ahû vairyô is a prayer, recited and worshipped as a statement affirming the law of holiness. It unfolds by identifying the law of holiness with the will of the Lord, then explaining that the will of the Lord is that law.

Ashem Vohû is a prayer, a statement and teaching that holiness is the best of all good. It is recited and repeatedly proclaimed in blessings, invocations, and ritual instruction with this explanation.

l: holy men and women, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: Holy men and women in Aryan, Turanian, Sairimyan, Sâini, Dâhi, and all countries, across generations, struggle for holiness and teach the Law; they are worshipped through their Fravashis, souls, spirits, consciences, and perceptions.
The primitive law is associated with the men who first listened to Ahura's teaching and struggled for holiness. Zarathustra is identified as a man of the primitive law.

Holiness is the best of all good. It is sought, praised, obtained, declared, worshipped, and victoriously maintained against fiends. Holy men and women and men of the primitive law seek it; king Vîstâspa maintains it, while friends of Astvat-ereta follow the good law. It is praised through Ashem Vohû, healing Words, and a recital praising Ahura Mazda and Mazda’s good things.

The material world is the realm in which Zarathustra is called lord and master and in which he worshipped Mãthra-Spenta. The material world is described as an abode full of cattle, wishes, and enjoyments of love, and as a decaying world contrasted with the world of the spirit.

l: Verethraghna, made by Ahura, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: Verethraghna appears in ten forms, including a strong wind, bull, horse, camel, boar, youth, raven, ram, buck, and armed man. He grants virility, bodily strength, health, keen sight, victory, and protection, and he confounds or destroys hostile forces.

Azi Dahâka is a powerful, fiendish Drug, three-mouthed, three-headed, six-eyed, and thousand-sensed, created by Angra Mainyu against the material and good world. He sacrifices to Vayu seeking to empty all seven Karshvares of men, but fails. He struggles with Âtar over the Glory and retreats when threatened. Thraêtaona seeks power to overcome him and ultimately kills him.

Vârengana is a strong feathered bird whose feathers and bones serve as protective talismans, bringing their holder help, homage, Glory, and protection; its feather is prescribed against curses or spells through rubbing or holding.

Haoma is a victorious, protective sacrifice: offered to Vayu, strained for sacrifice, and drunk with Asha and Ashi Vanguhi. It saves the head and body and grants battle victory. Honored with the Mãthra and Zarathustra, it sacrifices to Ashi Vanguhi and gains power to bind Franghrasyan for Husravah.

Vayu is a holy God belonging to Spenta Mainyu and the Good Spirit. Powerful beyond other creatures, he passes through two worlds as an overtaking, all-smiting worker of good, strong and golden-adorned. Worshipped by Ahura Mazda, he grants boons and protection to worthy worshippers, refuses Azi Dahâka’s request, and reveals many names.

is_granted_by Vayu [to worthy sacrificers] Boons are requested from Vayu for victory, protection, glory, prosperity, love, marriage, and other aims. Vayu grants the boons of Ahura Mazda, Haoshyangha, Takhma Urupa, Yima, Thraêtaona, Keresâspa, Aurvasâra, Hutaosa, and the maids, but refuses Azi Dahâka’s boon.

Kista is a holy, most right being made by Ahura Mazda and identified with the good Law. Swift, clever, renowned, cleansing, and protective, she supplies good stores, frees from dangers, and grants vital strengths and abilities.

The worshippers of Mazda are followers of Zarathustra who obey Ahura Mazda’s laws, hate Daêvas, and follow their Law. They worship through sacrifices, prayers, and glorifications, practice holiness, gain protection and spiritual knowledge, and seek prosperity and the defeat of the Drug.

is_a Yast [XVI] The Dîn Yast unit presents invocations, sacrifices, and praises directed toward Kista and the good Law of the worshippers of Mazda. It concludes with blessings and a request for brightness, glory, long life, and the blissful abode of the holy Ones.

Ahuna Vairya is a fiend-smiting, healing prayer and formula. Zarathustra sings and repeats it four times with increasing force; its Glory drives the Daêvas beneath the earth and removes sacrifice and prayer from them. Pronouncing it with the word of truth increases strength, victory, and piety in one's soul.

is_a Turanian murderer Franghrasyan is described as a Turanian murderer. Haoma receives the boon of binding and dragging him to Husravah, and Husravah receives the boon of killing him to avenge the deaths of Syâvarshâna and Aghraêratha.
The courtezan is a woman condemned for destroying her fruit, bearing a stranger’s child and presenting it to her husband; her untimely libations are rejected.

l: sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: Sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi includes ritual offerings, speech, deeds, and words; several figures offer it for glory, prosperity, victory, protection, and boons.

l: boon granted by Ashi Vanguhi, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: Ashi Vanguhi grants requested powers or benefits to petitioners, including Haoshyangha, Yima Khshaêta, Thraêtaona, Haoma, Husravah, Zarathustra, and Kavi Vîstâspa.

is_a Yast Âstâd Yast praises Ahura Mazda, the Aryan Glory, Ashi Vanguhi, Tistrya, holiness, and the law of holiness. It records teachings, praises, worship, and blessings connected with the Glory of the Aryas.

The Aryan Glory, made by Mazda or Ahura Mazda, is rich in food, flocks, wealth, intelligence, money, and glory. It withstands Need and enemies, destroys named fiends and non-Aryan nations, then brings increase to mountains, vales, and fair golden-hued growing plants, with victory, intelligence, and virtuous offspring.
Tistrya is a bright, glorious star whose movement brings increase, multiplying horses, flocks, and virtuous offspring, and is hailed with Mazda’s strong wind and Aryas’ Glory.

Ahura Mazda is a creator, Maker of the material and good world, Holy One, most beneficent Spirit, and source of Glory. He creates many good, fair, wonderful, prosperous, bright creatures, the Good Principle, kingly Glory, the Law of Mazda, and Zarathustra; he is father and commander of the Amesha-Spentas. Ever eager to create new creatures, he opposes Frangrasyan. His Holy Word is to be kept, studied, and spoken, and its faithful recitation praises Holiness, him, and his good creations. He protects faithful people, grants guidance, glory, healing, prosperity, and heavenly reward, and explains the souls’ destinations and nourishment after death, distinguishing faithful and wicked people.

The creation belongs to and is made prosperous by the Good Spirit. It is destined to become deathless; when the world is restored, it will no longer grow old, die, decay, or rot, while the Drug and her hundredfold brood perish.
Mount Haraiti Barez is the first mountain to rise from the earth, stretching east along shores of the land washed by waters.

is_a mountain [one of the mountains that grew up after Mount Zeredhô] Mount Ushi-dhau Ushi-darena is listed among the mountains that grew up after the first two mountains. It is also described as standing surrounded by waters near Lake Kãsava and the Haêtumant river.
Mount Ushi-darena, made by Mazda, is a mountain and seat of holy happiness, surrounded by waters and connected to where kingly Glory cleaves to one raised there.
is_the_source_of Astvat-ereta [place from which he rises] Lake Kãsava is the place from which Astvat-ereta will rise.

l: the Son of the Waters, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV
s: A swift-horsed, tall, shining male god beneath sea Vouru-Kasha seizes Glory, made and shaped man, and quickly hears worship.

is_a courage [firm of foot, unsleeping, quick to rise, and fully awake] Manly Courage claves unto Keresâspa and is described as firm of foot, unsleeping, quick to rise, and fully awake. It accompanies him in his acts of killing hostile beings.

Frangrasyan is a crafty Turanian ruffian who three times dives into sea Vouru-Kasha seeking the awful kingly Glory but fails. He threatens corn and liquors, bears Glory after Drvau and the Bull are killed, and is ultimately defeated and bound by Kavi Husravah.
